rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /(orthotic|orthoses|podiatry and immobilisation|prosthetic components|artificial limb|wheelchairs?|specialist seating|physiotherapy and occupational therapy|technology enabled care|electronic assistive technology|external breast prosthes)/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on. This patch is three services that share a commissioner and little else, and the frameworks above reflect that: two are its own (Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation; Prosthetic Components and Associated Products), two are shared with the Patient Moving and Handling page (Wheelchairs, Specialist Seating and Related Services; Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy), and the supplier counts on the shared ones are therefore borrowed rather than exclusive. No Drug Tariff panel is published here, and that is a finding rather than a gap: aggregating the whole of NHSBSA Prescription Cost Analysis for 2025/26 on 11/09/2026 returned £2,254 of prosthetic adhesives on 143 items, £25,707 of chiropody appliances and £9,863 of trusses across England for a full year. Prosthetics and orthotics are not reimbursed in the community; they are issued by a service against a framework. The compression and lymphoedema lines that do sit in Part IXA belong to the Tissue Viability and Wound Care page, which claims that part.
rules.suppliers: Every supplier NHS Supply Chain names on the frameworks above, resolved to one name per company through the Hub's alias registry, and ordered by how many of this speciality's frameworks they appear on. That count is the only claim made. It is not a ranking of size or share. Where NHS Supply Chain spelled a company two ways across its own pages, both spellings are shown against the one entry. This patch is three services that share a commissioner and little else, and the frameworks above reflect that: two are its own (Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation; Prosthetic Components and Associated Products), two are shared with the Patient Moving and Handling page (Wheelchairs, Specialist Seating and Related Services; Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy), and the supplier counts on the shared ones are therefore borrowed rather than exclusive. No Drug Tariff panel is published here, and that is a finding rather than a gap: aggregating the whole of NHSBSA Prescription Cost Analysis for 2025/26 on 11/09/2026 returned £2,254 of prosthetic adhesives on 143 items, £25,707 of chiropody appliances and £9,863 of trusses across England for a full year. Prosthetics and orthotics are not reimbursed in the community; they are issued by a service against a framework. The compression and lymphoedema lines that do sit in Part IXA belong to the Tissue Viability and Wound Care page, which claims that part.
rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(prosthetic(?:s)?|prosthes[ei]s|orthotic(?:s)?|orthos(?:is|es)|artificial limb(?:s)?|amputee(?:s)?|wheelchair(?:s)?|specialist seating|postural (?:seating|management|supports?|services?)|electronic assistive technology)\b/i and does not match /\b(aortic|mitral|heart valve|surgically implanted breast|wheelchair lift(?:s)?)\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality. A CPV code beginning 331931 or 331932 or 33183 is recorded as corroboration where the feed carries one, but never admits a notice on its own: a notice carrying a basket of CPV codes is filed under all of them and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: No Drug Tariff part applies to this speciality. Part IX reimburses dressings and elastic hosiery (IXA), incontinence appliances (IXB), stoma appliances (IXC) and elastic hosiery (IXR); nothing on this patch is listed there, so the panel carries no tariff rather than reaching for the nearest part.
rules.directorySuppliers: Companies the Hub's own supplier directory files under this speciality, from the speciality labels on each company's directory record, resolved through speciality-label-map.json and speciality-map.json (Compare ids: orthotics, rehab). They are labelled DIRECTORY-TAGGED because the tag is the Hub's filing of a company's range, not a procurement record: being listed here is not evidence of a contract or of volume, and the list is not a census of the market. A company that is also on this speciality's own frameworks is listed once, with the framework-named suppliers, and marked as also directory-tagged. WHERE A COMPANY IS ON ANOTHER FRAMEWORK: where a directory-tagged company is named on an NHS Supply Chain framework that is not counted as this speciality's, it is still listed, with that framework named against it and linked, so it is not lost from the page. 21 of the 24 listed here carry such a note. Framework names and links come from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs as held in frameworks.json; an agreement the directory records from another buying organisation, such as an NHS Shared Business Services framework, is shown as the directory states it.
rules.gpPrescribing: No BNF section is mapped to this speciality, so no GP prescribing market is sized here rather than borrowing a neighbouring page's.
rules.mhraDsu: Every MHRA Drug Safety Update that GOV.UK itself tags to a therapeutic area mapped to this speciality in config/mhra-dsu-speciality-map.json. The speciality comes only from GOV.UK's own facet, never from the title or the text. The monthly 'Letters and medicine recalls sent to healthcare professionals' roundup is left out (0 here), and so is any update GOV.UK ticks against 30 or more therapeutic areas, which is a message to everyone rather than to this speciality (3 here). Newest first; the count is every tagged update in the archive, and the list shows the most recent. MHRA Drug Safety Update, GOV.UK, as at 2026-11-26.

localIntel.org: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
localIntel.title: Wheelchair and Postural Services, North Yorkshire and York, awarded to Blatchford Limited
localIntel.fact: Blatchford Limited is the named supplier on the award for Wheelchair and Postural Services for North Yorkshire and York. The ICB ran an open procedure under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, with a tender value of £15,250,000. The notice records no contract start or end date and no award value, so the term is not verified.
localIntel.quote: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (ICB), hereafter the Relevant Authority, is seeking to commission Wheelchair and Postural Services for North Yorkshire and York through a Competitive Process under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023.
localIntel.use: Names the incumbent for wheelchairs and postural seating across North Yorkshire and York, and the size of the service at £15.25m. A supplier selling seating or postural equipment into this patch sells through Blatchford, not to the ICB.

localIntel.title: Integrated Clinical Mobility Service (Wheelchairs and Orthotics) in Northamptonshire, awarded to Blatchford Limited
localIntel.fact: Blatchford Limited is the named supplier on the award for a countywide all-age integrated orthotics, wheelchair and posture service in Northamptonshire. The notice records the procedure as an award procedure without prior publication of a call for competition. No value, start date or end date is given on the notice, so none of those is verified.
localIntel.quote: Provision of a countywide all age integrated high quality, responsive and safe orthotics, wheelchair and posture service that maximises mobility and independence through timely access to both initial assessment and review of individual need, including the provision, and ongoing repair or maintenance where required, of appropriate clinically identified equipment.
localIntel.use: Orthotics and wheelchairs are commissioned together here, under one provider, and awarded without competition. A rep covering Northamptonshire has one door, Blatchford, for both product groups.

localIntel.org: NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board
localIntel.title: Dudley Wheelchair Assessment and Equipment Service, awarded to AJM Healthcare
localIntel.ends: 30/09/2029, option to extend up to a further 2 years
localIntel.fact: AJM Healthcare holds the Wheelchair Assessment and Equipment Service for patients registered with a Dudley GP. The award records £6,749,999 against an above-threshold open procedure, running three years from 1 October 2026 to 30 September 2029, with the Commissioner holding an option to extend for up to a further two years. The award entity is recorded both as AJM Healthcare and as AJM Healthcare Group Limited.
localIntel.quote: As a result of this above threshold open procedure process, a Contract has been entered into with the Most Advantageous Tender supplier for a period of 3 Years commencing on 01st October 2026, with the Commissioner having the option to extend the contract for up to a further 2 years.
localIntel.use: The Dudley service changed hands with effect from 1 October 2026. Any wheelchair or postural product going into Dudley now goes through AJM Healthcare, and the first re-let point is autumn 2029.

localIntel.org: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
localIntel.title: Specialist Mobility and Rehabilitation Centre wheelchair maintenance and refurbishment, awarded to AJM Healthcare
localIntel.fact: A J Mobility Limited, trading as AJM Healthcare, holds wheelchair maintenance and refurbishment for the trust's Specialist Mobility and Rehabilitation Centre, covering Lancashire and South Cumbria. The award value is £10,150,000 against a tender value of £10,500,000, and the contract period runs 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032. The procedure is recorded as a competitive flexible procedure.
localIntel.quote: Wheelchair maintenance and refurbishment services for LSC
localIntel.use: Maintenance and refurbishment is a separate five-year contract from assessment and supply, and it is already let to 2032. Taken with Dudley, it shows AJM Healthcare holding both service and maintenance work in two unconnected patches.

localIntel.org: Business Services Organisation, Procurement and Logistics Service (PaLS)
localIntel.title: Postural Management Equipment and Accessories framework for Northern Ireland
localIntel.fact: PaLS awarded a Northern Ireland framework for the supply and delivery of postural management equipment and accessories through an open procedure, running 1 November 2026 to 31 October 2030. The tender value is £26,000,000 and each of the eight lot awards records £3,170,000. Ten suppliers appear across the lots: Accora (Ireland) Ltd, BES Healthcare Ltd, Evolution Healthcare, James Leckey Design, John Preston & Co (Belfast) Ltd, LC Seating Limited, Moorings Mediquip UK Ltd, Primacy Healthcare 21 Ltd, Sync Living Ltd and Primacy Healthcare 21 Limited as a second recorded entity. No single supplier appears on all eight lots.
localIntel.quote: Business Services Organisation (BSO), Procurement and Logistics Service (PaLS) sought through this tender opportunity to establish a Framework for the for the supply and delivery of Postural Management Equipment and Accessories
localIntel.use: The national route into Northern Ireland for postural seating until October 2030, and the lot pattern says which competitor can sell what there. A supplier not on it has no PaLS route for four years.

localIntel.title: Orthotics Products and Services including Prosthetic Services framework: the route trusts use, and its end date
localIntel.fact: The NHS SBS portfolio dated 30/06/2026 lists the Orthotics Products and Services including Prosthetic Services Framework Agreement with a maximum end date of 08/10/2027 and says it covers stock, modular and bespoke products across nine lots for upper and lower body orthoses for adult and paediatric patients. The Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital award notice describes the same framework (reference SBS10247) as three lots: orthotic products, orthotic services and prosthetic services. The portfolio does not name the suppliers on each lot, and the nine-lot and three-lot descriptions are not reconciled here: the supplier list per lot is not verified.
localIntel.quote: The Orthotics Products and Services including Prosthetic Services Framework Agreement allows for the provision of stock, modular and bespoke products. Nine lots cover upper and lower body orthoses for adult and paediatric patients.
localIntel.use: Names the national route for orthotic and prosthetic buying and the date it runs out. A trust buying through a further competition (as RNOH did) is buying under this framework, so a supplier outside it needs to be on the re-let. Get the lot and supplier list from NHS SBS before quoting it to a customer.

localIntel.org: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust
localIntel.title: Provision of Prosthetic and Orthotic Services, awarded to Hugh Steeper Limited (t/a Steeper) under NHS SBS SBS10247
localIntel.fact: Hugh Steeper Limited (t/a Steeper) is the named supplier, the only one on the notice, after a further competition under the NHS SBS Orthotics Products and Services including Prosthetic Services framework (reference SBS10247). Three bids were received. The contract value is £6,369,486.54 and it was signed on 03/09/2026. The trust awarded one contract to one supplier covering all three lots. The notice describes the full term as seven years with two optional 12-month extensions; no start or end date is recorded on the notice, so the end date is not verified. The notice's lot record carries the status 'cancelled' while the award and contract are 'active'; what that status means is not verified.
localIntel.quote: The Authority will award a single contract to a single supplier covering all three (3) Lots.
localIntel.use: The RNOH prosthetic, orthotic products and orthotic services spend sits with one supplier for the seven-year term, so a rep selling orthotic devices or prosthetic components here sells through Steeper, not to the trust.

localIntel.org: Ministry of Defence (Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre)
localIntel.title: Prosthetics and Orthotics Rehabilitation Service at DMRC: four-year contract from 01/04/2027, tender closed
localIntel.fact: The Ministry of Defence published an open-procedure tender for an on-site prosthetic and orthotic rehabilitation service at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre, estimated at £8,736,000 excluding VAT (£10,100,000 including VAT). The contract period runs 01/04/2027 to 31/03/2031 with an option to extend by up to 24 months to 31/03/2033. Award weighting is 50% cost and 50% technical. Tenders closed on 07/10/2026. The record carries no award, so the winning supplier is not verified. The contractor must supply its own prosthetic and orthotic management IT system.
localIntel.quote: The authority is seeking to tender for a 4 -year contract to start on 01 Apr 2027, with the option to extend up to 24 months.
localIntel.use: A live prosthetic and orthotic service contract of about £8.7m ex VAT starting 01/04/2027, with the winner not yet on the record. Watch Find a Tender for the award; the contractor must also supply a prosthetic and orthotic management IT system, which is a possible route for a digital supplier.

localIntel.org: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust, with RJAH and Shropshire Community Health NHS Trust
localIntel.title: Orthotic Splints and Braces: joint tender for 2027, closed 13/11/2026
localIntel.fact: Three Shropshire-area buyers (Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital, the Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Orthopaedic Hospital and Shropshire Community Health) are named on one below-threshold open tender, valued at £60,135.88 excluding VAT, for a contract period of 01/01/2027 to 31/12/2027. Tenders closed on 13/11/2026. The notice records no award, so the supplier is not verified, and the lot is marked as suitable for SMEs. Award criteria are in attached documents that were not read, so the weighting is not verified.
localIntel.quote: Orthotic Splints & Braces - RJAH, SATH , SCT
localIntel.use: Shows three Shropshire-area buyers pooling orthotic splint and brace spend into one one-year contract running to 31/12/2027. Watch Find a Tender for the award, which names who supplies all three.

localIntel.org: The Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
localIntel.title: Orthotic Footwear consumables: four-year contract from 01/11/2026, tender closed 14/09/2026
localIntel.fact: RJAH published a below-threshold open competition for orthotic footwear consumables, valued at £17,564 excluding VAT (£21,076.80 including VAT), contract period 01/11/2026 to 31/10/2030. Tenders closed on 14/09/2026. The notice records no award, so the supplier is not verified, and the lot is marked as suitable for SMEs. Award criteria are in attached documents that were not read, so the weighting is not verified.
localIntel.use: A small contract, but a four-year one, that fixes who supplies RJAH's orthotic footwear until late 2030. Useful for a footwear supplier deciding whether the trust is worth a call; the value is under £18k over the whole term.

localIntel.org: NHS Surrey and Sussex Integrated Care Board
localIntel.title: Wheelchair and Specialist Seating Service (C401025), Sussex, awarded to AJ Mobility Ltd (trading as AJM Healthcare)
localIntel.ends: 31/03/2032 (initial term; 2-year extension to 31/03/2034 is an option)
localIntel.fact: AJ Mobility Ltd (Trading as AJM Healthcare) is the named supplier on the award. The notice gives a 5-year contract with an option to extend for 2 years, service dates 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032 and an extension to 31 March 2034, an annual contract value of £8,436,258 and a total value of £59,053,806 including the option. The record shows the contract signed on 09/06/2026. The notice is headed as a notification of intention to award; whether any standstill or challenge followed is not verified. The service covers manual and powered wheelchairs, pressure-relieving cushions and postural management equipment, with specialist static postural seating for adults in East Sussex only.
localIntel.quote: Contract length: 5-year contract with an option to extend for a further 2-years.
localIntel.use: The Sussex wheelchair, cushion and postural patch goes to AJM from 01/04/2027, so an equipment supplier selling into it will be selling through AJM, not the ICB. Who provides the service until then is not verified.
names: AJ Mobility Ltd (Trading as AJM Healthcare)

localIntel.org: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent Integrated Care Board
localIntel.title: Provision of Wheelchair Services, Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent, awarded to Ross Auto Engineering Limited (trading as Ross Care)
localIntel.ends: not verified (3 years from 01/10/2026 with up to 2 more; no end date is stated)
localIntel.fact: Ross Auto Engineering Limited (trading as Ross Care) is the named supplier on the award. NHS Midlands and Lancashire CSU ran a Provider Selection Regime competitive process on behalf of the ICB; submissions closed on 22 October 2025. The notice gives 3 years plus an optional 2, commencing 1 October 2026, a total awardable value of £12,676,460 including the extension, and says this is an existing service offered to a new provider. The outgoing provider is not named on the notice, so it is not verified. The record shows the contract signed on 23/02/2026. No end date is stated.
localIntel.quote: The Authority are looking to appoint a Service Provider, or Consortium, to deliver this Service for a period of 3 Years with the option to extend for up to a further 2 years. The Contract will commence on the 1st October 2026.
localIntel.use: The provider changes on 01/10/2026, per the notice. A new provider mobilising a service is a point at which it may review its equipment, repair and seating suppliers, so Ross Care is the door, not the ICB.
names: Ross Auto Engineering Limited (trading as Ross Care)

localIntel.org: NHS North East London Integrated Care Board
localIntel.title: NHS NEL ICB Integrated Wheelchair Service, awarded to A J Mobility Ltd
localIntel.fact: A J Mobility Ltd is the named supplier on the award for an integrated wheelchair service for all ages across Barking, Havering, Redbridge, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest. The record shows a contract value of £26,385,099.65 and a contract signed on 01/07/2025. The notice describes wheelchair supply, rehabilitation engineering facilities and service and maintenance packages. No start date, end date or extension is stated on the notice, so the term is not verified.
localIntel.quote: NHS North East London Integrated Care Board (NEL ICB) has commissioned an integrated wheelchair service for people of all ages who have a long-term need for mobility assistance in Barking, Havering, Redbridge, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest.
localIntel.use: Five north-east London boroughs buy wheelchairs, rehabilitation engineering and maintenance as one package from AJM, so a rehabilitation engineering or repair supplier would be approaching AJM, not the ICB. Any subcontract arrangement is not verified.

localIntel.org: NHS Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Integrated Care Board
localIntel.title: Provision of Wheelchair and Posture Services for Children, Young People and Adults (Standard and Specialised), awarded to Ross Auto Engineering Limited t/a Ross Care
localIntel.ends: not verified (5 years with an option of up to 5 more; no end date is stated)
localIntel.fact: Ross Auto Engineering Limited t/a Ross Care is the named supplier on the award. The notice is an intention to award under the Provider Selection Regime. It gives a 5-year contract with an option to extend for up to a further 5 years, an anticipated go-live of 1 April 2026 and an approximate lifetime value including the extension of £25,073,351, and says an existing service is being re-commissioned and awarded to a new provider. The record shows the contract signed on 16/01/2026. The outgoing provider is not named, and no end date is stated.
localIntel.quote: The contract will be for a period of 5 years with the option to extend for up to a further 5 year period.
localIntel.use: Ross Care appears on this award and on the Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent award under the same Companies House number, 00469301. A supplier using Ross Care as its route to market has two ICB footprints to cover.
names: Ross Auto Engineering Limited t/a Ross Care

localIntel.org: NHS Supply Chain (Supply Chain Coordination Limited)
localIntel.title: Wheelchairs, Specialist Seating and Related Services framework, 27 suppliers on Lot 1 and 7 on Lot 2
localIntel.ends: not verified (the notice states no framework term)
localIntel.fact: The notice establishes a framework with two lots: Lot 1, Wheelchairs and Specialist Seating Products (powered and manual wheelchairs, specialist seating systems and wheelbases, paediatric buggies, accessories and cushions) and Lot 2, Wheelchair Managed Services (repairs and maintenance, fully managed wheelchair service and wheelchair loan service). The notice records 27 suppliers on Lot 1 and 7 on Lot 2 and contract values of £50,000,000 for Lot 1 and £27,000,000 for Lot 2. The framework term is not verified. Estimated purchases in the first 12 months are given as circa £19,250,000 (approximate only).
localIntel.quote: NHS Supply Chain seeks to establish a Framework for the supply of Wheelchairs, Specialist Seating and Related Services.
localIntel.use: This is the national route for wheelchair and seating products and for managed services. Lot 2 names AJ Mobility, Blatchford and Ross Auto Engineering, the same suppliers that hold the local ICB wheelchair services in this desk. Whether a given local service buys through the framework is not verified.

localIntel.org: Business Services Organisation, Procurement and Logistics Service (PaLS)
localIntel.title: External Breast Prosthesis framework for Northern Ireland trusts, five lots, awarded to Amoena, Trulife, Boost Innovations and Iskus Health
localIntel.fact: The notice records an open procedure for a closed framework agreement, with and without reopening of competition, in five lots. Each lot's contract runs 1 August 2026 to 31 July 2028, with renewal of any period up to and including 24 months and a maximum extent of 31 July 2030. Lot 1 Full Breast Prostheses (Amoena (UK) Limited, Trulife Ltd, Boost Innovations Limited) is recorded at £1,128,703.13; Lot 2 Partial Breast Prostheses (Amoena, Trulife) at £129,591; Lot 3 Soft Form Prostheses (Amoena, Trulife) at £317,625; Lot 4 Leisure Prostheses (Amoena, Trulife, Boost Innovations) at £31,878; Lot 5 Bras (Amoena, Trulife, Iskus Health Ltd) at £12,808.13. The earlier market engagement notice named the Belfast, Western, South Eastern, Southern and Northern Health and Social Care Trusts; the award notice says only 'participating Trusts', so which trusts call off is not verified.
localIntel.quote: Procurement for the Supply and Delivery of External Breast Prosthesis for use across participating Trusts.
localIntel.use: This is the Northern Ireland route for breast prostheses until at least July 2028. Amoena and Trulife are on every lot and Boost Innovations and Iskus Health each hold a narrower slice, so a supplier outside these four has no framework route before the extension decision.

localIntel.title: UK Rehabilitation Outcomes Collective (UKROC) database, directly awarded to London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
localIntel.fact: NHS England recorded a direct award for the UK Rehabilitation Outcomes Collective (UKROC) database to London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust. The stated rationale is 'Technical reasons intellectual property'. The contract runs 29 September 2026 to 31 March 2027, with a 1 x 12 month option to extend (maximum extent 31 March 2028). The contract record gives £378,698 (ex VAT) and £770,272 (gross); how the two figures relate is not verified. The notice does not say which rehabilitation services must submit data to UKROC, so any link to specialised rehabilitation commissioning is not verified.
localIntel.use: UKROC is the national rehabilitation outcomes database and it is held by one NHS trust under a direct award, so it is a data source and not an open route. A supplier of rehabilitation equipment or services cannot buy into it; the term shows when NHS England next decides who holds it.
names: LONDON NORTH WEST UNIVERSITY HEALTHCARE NHS TRUST

localIntel.title: Amputee rehabilitation and prosthetics services for people of all ages with limb loss and limb difference, service specification D01/S/d
localIntel.ends: not verified (the specification states no end date)
localIntel.fact: NHS England published a revised service specification (number D01/S/d - 250502, May 2025) that replaces the 2016 version. It estimates 55,000 to 60,000 people in England with amputation or limb difference, with about 25,000 seen by prosthetic services each year, and a catchment of 1 to 2 million people per specialist prosthetic centre. Every service must have an on-site workshop to fabricate, repair and maintain prostheses. The only named outcome metric is a Socket Comfort Score of 7 or more on delivery of a new socket. High activity and competitive sport prostheses are not routinely commissioned. Microprocessor knees and multi-grip hands are governed by separate clinical commissioning policies. Section 7.8 says: 'The list of commissioned providers for the services covered by this specification will be published in due course.' The list of commissioned centres is therefore not verified.
localIntel.quote: This revised service specification has been updated and replaces the 2016 version.
localIntel.use: This is the document an NHS England-commissioned prosthetic centre is held to. Component and device supply has to fit an on-site workshop model and the socket comfort measure, and microprocessor and multi-grip products sit behind their own policies, so a rep should read the relevant policy before pitching either.

localIntel.org: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust
localIntel.title: Managed Service for Orthotics (WPL06521), interim direct award to Peacocks Medical Group Limited
localIntel.fact: The notice is an Intention to Award under the Provider Selection Regime, Direct Award Process C, to the incumbent Peacocks Medical Group Limited. The service covers orthotic clinics and ward consultations at Southampton General Hospital and Royal South Hants Hospital, manufacture and supply of custom and stock orthoses, an on-site workshop and inventory management. The interim term is 10 months from 1 December 2026 to 30 September 2027 with an optional 6 month extension, and the approximate lifetime value including the extension is £2,720,000 excluding VAT. The notice says the term is a bridge while the trust reviews the scope of the orthotic service with the ICB. The lot status field in the record reads 'cancelled' while the award reads 'active'; which applies is not verified. What replaces the interim contract is not verified.
localIntel.quote: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (UHS) intends to award a new contract directly to Peacocks Medical Group Ltd for the managed service for orthotics.
localIntel.use: Orthotics at this trust stays with the incumbent to September 2027 (March 2028 if extended) and a scope review with the ICB is under way, so the next opening is the re-let after that review, not this award.

gpPrescribing.scope: Items prescribed in primary care in England (GP practices and other prescribers NHSBSA attributes to a practice) and dispensed in the community, aggregated to ICB. Not hospital in-patient use, and not the trust-level hospital prescribing dataset.
gpPrescribing.whyEmpty: No BNF section is mapped to this speciality, so no GP prescribing market is sized here rather than borrowing a neighbouring page's.
